summary: Current main still used a 2x EAGLE KV reservation based on kv_committed_len, which lags target execution under overlap. The candidate sizes EAGLE allocation and its capacity check from synchronous host sequence lengths with a 1x per-decode reserve, while retaining the existing 2x behavior for UNO and other committed-watermark callers. A regression fails on the recorded base and passes after the change.

remaining_limitations: The reported GLM-5.2 744B MoE DSA NVFP4 weights, EAGLE draft model, eight B200 CUDA GPUs, and TP8 environment were unavailable, so the original cache-hit-rate and TTFT workload was not reproduced.

The supplied deterministic tiny Llama fixture validates transport and ordinary engine execution only and has no EAGLE draft checkpoint; using it could not qualify this speculative-decoding defect, so no startup smoke is claimed as issue evidence.
The change is therefore a source-level candidate backed by failing-before/passing-after allocator regression evidence, not a full-model performance validation.
The broad memory-cache suite has eight environment failures unrelated to this patch, and speculative unit collection requires unavailable FlashInfer.
